    This year, for my Thanksgiving story, I’m writing something experimental. I’ll treat the art of our country in 1863. That’s the year President Lincoln issued his proclamation designating the last Thursday in November as a national day of “Thanksgiving and Praise to our beneficent Father, who dwelleth in the Heavens.”.

    I’m an art historian and don’t believe that artists quaff a surfeit of blood-orange champagne mules, sing “Auld Lang Syne,” do a countdown if they’re sober enough to count backward, and decide — snap — to change styles or themes. That year — 1863 — was different, though, and that Thanksgiving was different. Eastman Johnson (1824–1906) was our savviest painter, tuned to the moment and its nuances.

    Sources indicate that brian T. Allen is National Review’s art critic.

    SolarEdge unveils U.S.-made optimizer for C&I solar

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • SolarEdge’s latest Duo Power Optimizer promises to simplify commercial and industrial solar installations with 50% fewer optimizer units, independent module-level power tracking, and enhanced safety features.
    • The commercial and industrial (C&I) solar market is getting a fresh hardware option aimed at making installations simpler without sacrificing system performance.
    • Unveiled November 16 ahead of RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, the new product introduces a 2:1 architecture that allows one optimizer to connect two solar modules.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    SolarEdge’s latest Duo Power Optimizer promises to simplify commercial and industrial solar installations with 50% fewer optimizer units, independent module-level power tracking, and enhanced safety features.

    The commercial and industrial (C&I) solar market is getting a fresh hardware option aimed at making installations simpler without sacrificing system performance. SolarEdge Technologies has unveiled its new Duo Power Optimizer, a U.S.-manufactured solution designed to deliver module-level energy harvesting and monitoring while cutting the number of power optimizers in half.

    Unveiled November 16 ahead of RE+ 2026 in Las Vegas, the new product introduces a 2:1 architecture that allows one optimizer to connect two solar modules. Notably, each module retains its own independent maximum power point tracker (MPPT), which preserves the module-level performance benefits associated with the traditional one-to-one optimizer configurations.

    For developers, EPCs and installers managing large-scale rooftop and distributed generation projects, the value here lies in fewer components to purchase, wire and install, with no trade-off in module-level optimization.

    Simplifying installation without sacrificing performance.

    It has been revealed that solarEdge’s optimization tech addresses the challenge of conventional string inverter systems, which is that an underperforming module can affect the output of an entire string. But by allowing each module to operate independently, the system limits the impact of shading, degradation or performance differences between panels.

    In a recent development, the Duo brings demonstrates that capability in a two-module configuration. By reducing the number of optimizers by 50% compared with one-to-one designs, SolarEdge is targeting an opportunity to streamline balance-of-system requirements and reduce the installation labor.

    In a recent development, solarEdge’s U.S.-made Duo Power Optimizer connects two solar modules while maintaining independent module-level power tracking for commercial and industrial solar installations. Credit: SolarEdge.

    Sources indicate that the hardware also incorporates design changes intended to improve jobsite efficiency. Each optimizer features two input pairs: a shorter connection for the nearest module and a pre-extended connection for the adjacent module. The arrangement reduces excess wiring and eliminates the need for field-made jumpers.

    The configuration also accommodates modules with different orientations, making it particularly relevant for east-west and dual-tilt racking applications.

    Safety moves closer to the module.

    Beyond installation efficiency, SolarEdge is emphasizing electrical safety as a central feature of the upcoming product.

    The Duo extends the manufacturer’s Sense Connect technology to its input and output connectors, monitoring connector temperatures to identify developing challenges before they potentially escalate into overheating or electrical arcs.

    It has been revealed that also, the optimizer introduces what SolarEdge describes as an industry-first approach to arc fault detection: every optimizer acts as an individual arc sensor. Rather than relying exclusively on detection at the inverter, the system distributes monitoring throughout the array, allowing potential arc faults to be identified closer to their source.

    Industry observers note that solarEdge states the technology provides coverage across strings with up to 3,280 feet of total cable length between the inverter and optimizer. It can also help pinpoint problems to the optimizer area, potentially making troubleshooting and maintenance more efficient.

    Recent findings suggest that manufactured at SolarEdge’s Florida facility, the Duo is designed to meet U.S. Domestic Content and Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) requirements, according to the manufacturer. SolarEdge says its domestic-content eligibility levels are consistent with those of its previous U.S.-manufactured power optimizers, subject to applicable tax guidance and project-specific requirements.

    A practical play for the C&I market.

    For SolarEdge, the Duo represents an effort to combine three priorities that are becoming more and more notable in commercial solar: installation efficiency, system-level safety, and domestic manufacturing.

    The technology does not fundamentally change the value proposition of module-level optimization. Instead, it looks to make that architecture more economical and easier to deploy at scale.

    SolarEdge will showcase the Duo Power Optimizer at RE+ 2026.

    In 2023 New York began barring Airbnb and other platforms from processing unregistered bookings. For stays under 30 days, the host generally has to stay in the apartment and can take only two paying guests. That limits supply but makes the argument for new hotels even stronger, but those are effectively barred too.

    Industry observers note that A study in the European Journal of Political Economy estimated that the short-term rental crackdown added $14 to $19 to the average hotel night. Hotels took in an estimated $2.1 billion to $2.9 billion more over the first 18 months while selling roughly the same number of nights.

    A family that cuts a three-night New York trip to two buys one fewer dinner. Another goes somewhere else instead. Or they do the full New York trip but spend less while they’re there. Restaurants see less money. There are fewer restaurant jobs, and tip income for waiters goes down.     #169845. GAO chief nominee triggers partisan clash at Senate hearing

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1223 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    GAO chief nominee triggers partisan clash at Senate hearing

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1223 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that eric Ueland, nominee to be comptroller general, sits at the witness table for his confirmation hearing with the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday.
    • Eric Ueland, President Donald Trump’s pick for comptroller general, promised to be independent and impartial if confirmed, amid criticism from Democrats and outside groups, during a confirmation hearing Thursday.
    • “I’m not here as a plant, a stooge, a lackey for anybody,” he told Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., after Democrats on the panel accused him of being a “rubber stamp” for the administration.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that eric Ueland, nominee to be comptroller general, sits at the witness table for his confirmation hearing with the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee on Thursday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Eric Ueland, President Donald Trump’s pick for comptroller general, promised to be independent and impartial if confirmed, amid criticism from Democrats and outside groups, during a confirmation hearing Thursday.

    “I’m not here as a plant, a stooge, a lackey for anybody,” he told Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Chairman Rand Paul, R-Ky., after Democrats on the panel accused him of being a “rubber stamp” for the administration.

    In a recent development, democrats have criticized Ueland, a longtime GOP Senate aide and administration official during both Trump terms, saying he is too politically biased to lead the nonpartisan watchdog agency which conducts investigations and audits for Congress. They also stated Republicans ignored a law that Democrats say requires the convening of a special legislative commission to make recommendations for the post.

    According to recent reports, ueland said if the Senate confirms him to lead the Government Accountability Office, “We can at the end of the day ... see a GAO which is more effective, which provides better information for Congress in a quicker way so Congress is able to take policy actions and drive change itself at this end of Pennsylvania Avenue.”.

    At the root of the partisan clash is a suspicion by Democrats that Trump is trying to install a puppet to lead an agency that has fought the administration repeatedly over the power of the purse and other matters.

    Democrats blasted Paul for rushing the hearing, which included a dozen other nominees for administration and judicial posts.

    “It’s so apparent that this is a box-checking exercise,” said Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan, the ranking Democrat on the panel. “This committee is not doing due diligence, despite some of our members’ best efforts, because the chairman has chosen not to carry out his responsibility to provide advice and consent on nominations.”.

    Democrats said Paul did not allow Peters to make an opening statement at the hearing and restricted the amount of time given to senators to ask questions. A GOP aide disputed this, noting that Paul did not give an opening statement himself, Peters arrived late and all senators were given five minutes to ask questions.

    Industry observers note that ueland has served as deputy director for management at the Office of Management and Budget under Russ Vought, the OMB director. Trump nominated Ueland to head the GAO, a legislative branch agency, Monday.

    In a recent development, democrats noted that the GAO has concluded multiple times that the administration violated the law by "impounding," or refusing to spend, appropriated funds. OMB has argued that the GAO misread the law and that it does not have any authority over the executive branch.

    Peters told Ueland that the GAO had issued 12 reports accusing the administration of violating the law, and he asked if Ueland agreed.

    Ueland did not give a direct response.

    “First, many of those items indicated by those reports, I have not participated in,” he stated. Ueland said he had not reviewed the reports that Peters provided to him earlier, and that he would not offer an opinion on them.

    He also remarked it was critical that he “not prejudge or come to this committee with informed conclusions about what it is that GAO has rendered as advice to Congress.” Ueland said he has a “clear commitment to follow the process.”.

    Peters stated when Ueland appeared before the committee last year after being nominated for the OMB post, he voiced support for the presidential authority of impoundment.

    Recent findings suggest that “We’re going to expect you to continue to basically ignore Congress,” Peters said. “You’re going to be a rubber stamp for the administration.”.

    “That’s not so,” Ueland replied.

    Ueland said his experience as deputy overseeing the management side of OMB would be a “value add to GAO.” He cited his work “examining how the government actually functions, how it is organized, how it can be better optimized to deliver results.”.

    Industry observers note that sen. Bernie Moreno, R-Ohio, asked Ueland how he would grade GAO’s work to date.

    Ueland said he would give it a “medium grade over time.”.

    For example, he said GAO has 38 government operations on a “high-risk list … some of which have been on there for 36 years.”.

    By contrast, Ueland referred to his work at OMB, where he said “you have seen a very swift and aggressive effort by this administration in this term to set up systems and processes to ensure that we are not sending money out the door that we shouldn’t.”.

    Paul asked Ueland what he would do if administration officials told him they did not like a GAO investigation or conclusion.

    Ueland stated he would “fully follow through on charges from Congress and in the event of obstacles figure out ways to proceed to try to elicit information.” He said when he was a young staffer in the Senate, when there were disagreements between the legislative and executive branches, GAO and the administration had conversations “to see if there were appropriate paths forward.”.

    Responding to another question from Paul as to whether he would ignore a potential request from the White House to stop an investigation, Ueland said, “To be clear, yes.”.

    Industry observers note that sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., who is seeking to be the ranking Republican on the committee in the next Congress, mentioned he was satisfied that Republicans followed the letter of the law requiring a commission to make recommendations to the president for comptroller general. He added that he was not “completely sure they have followed the entire spirit of the law.”.

    “For me, personally, Mr. Ueland is a great candidate in this role for GAO,” Lankford remarked.

    Industry observers note that paul sent three recommendations for comptroller general, including Ueland, to the White House last week from the six Republican members of a 10-member bipartisan, bicameral commission. But he never convened the body to seek applications from and interview candidates for the post.

    And he gave the four Democrats on the commission less than 24 hours’ notice last week to offer their recommendations. Democrats charged that Paul subverted the process, and they did not offer recommendations.

    In a separate interview Wednesday, the president of the union that represents GAO employees decried the decision not to follow the commission process that characterized past comptroller general nominations.

    “We see that bipartisan process as extremely key to preserving and keeping the trust that GAO has with the entire Congress,” said Benjamin Emmel, president of Local 1921 of the International Federation of Professionals and Technical Engineers.

    Emmel, a senior analyst at GAO, said by sidestepping that procedure, “there is a cloud that hangs above any nominee where one party dominates that process.”.

    According to recent reports, he said GAO’s credibility depends on members of both parties trusting that the organization is “nonpartisan, objective, independent and fair. If we lose that ability, we become less useful.”.

    In a recent development, the union is not advocating for or against Ueland or any nominee for the office. The Homeland Security panel is not expected to vote on the nominations until after Thanksgiving.

    Citi AAdvantage Business Card Review—75,000 Miles And Status Credit For Two People From The Same Spending

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 44 min read (8749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~44 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read

    • Industry observers note that I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog.
    • It has been revealed that the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] can turn $125,000 in eligible spending on an employee card into American Airlines Platinum Pro status for two people.
    • The Citi AAdvantage Business Card is the best airline credit card for spending toward status.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that I receive compensation for content and many links on this blog. Be aware that websites may earn compensation when a customer clicks on a link, when an application is approved, or when an account is opened. Citibank is an advertising partner of this site, as is American Express, Chase, Capital One, and others. Any opinions expressed in this post are my own, and have not been reviewed, approved, or endorsed by my advertising partners. I do not write about all offers that are available -- instead focusing on miles, points, and cash back (and currencies that can be converted into the same). Terms apply to the offers and benefits listed on this page.

    It has been revealed that the Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® [See rates and fees] can turn $125,000 in eligible spending on an employee card into American Airlines Platinum Pro status for two people. That’s without even earning any Loyalty Points from flying, a hotel booking or shopping through American’s portal.

    The Citi AAdvantage Business Card is the best airline credit card for spending toward status. I have the card, and I’m keeping it. The limited-time initial bonus is strong, the first year has no annual fee, and the recently announced refresh adds benefits. But the reason to put spending on this card is that two people can get status credit for the same purchases.

    In a recent development, the current limited time offer is 75,000 American Airlines AAdvantage bonus miles after $5,000 in purchases within the first five months of account opening. Purchases by the primary cardmember and employees count toward that requirement. There’s no annual fee for the first 12 months. The card’s regular annual fee is currently $99, but it rises to $150 with renewals beginning January 24, 2027. Someone opening the card now will see a $150 annual fee at renewal. Employee cards have no additional annual fee, and there’s no foreign transaction fee. The initial bonus alone can cover a one way Japan Airlines business class award between the U.S. and Japan when partner award space is available. American miles remain especially strong for premium cabin awards on partners. Prices largely remain at the same level they were a decade ago, while numerous other progams have devalued. Citi’s 48 month restriction applies to an initial bonus on this business card, including its former CitiBusiness AAdvantage Platinum Select-named product. Citi also restricts eligibility after converting another Citi account with a recent initial bonus into this product. Having a separate personal American Airlines card doesn’t, by itself, disqualify you. How The Same Citi AAdvantage Business Card Spending Earns Status For Two People Normally each cardmember earns one Loyalty Point per dollar on their purchases. When an employee uses their card, those Loyalty Points go to the employee. Through December 31, 2028, the primary cardmember also receives one Loyalty Point per dollar of eligible employee card spending. That’s an additional credit to a second person’s account. Spending on the primary cardmember’s card still earns that person one Loyalty Point per dollar. When I covered the refresh, American confirmed to me that all Citi AAdvantage Business cardmembers were included after the former Barclays business accounts migrated. This used to be called a targeted promotion because legacy Barclays cardmembers didn’t qualify. Here’s what eligible spending on one employee’s card can accomplish in a single status qualification year, assuming neither person earns Loyalty Points elsewhere: Employee Card Spending Primary Cardmember Employee $40,000 Gold Gold $75,000 Platinum Platinum $125,000 Platinum Pro Platinum Pro $200,000 Executive Platinum Executive Platinum American’s qualification year starts March 1 and runs through the end of February. You can combine the card’s Loyalty Points with qualifying activity from other sources. A business owner with several employee cards receives the additional Loyalty Points across their eligible spending. Each employee gets credit for the purchases on their individual card. Authorized users must be employees or contractors of the business, and need to be enrolled in AAdvantage and AAdvantage Business to receive their Loyalty Points. A spouse who works in the business fits this. The Business Controls The Miles Redeemable miles work differently from status credit. The miles from purchases, including employee purchases, and the initial bonus go into the company’s AAdvantage Business account. The business can then transfer miles to registered travelers’ personal AAdvantage accounts, including the primary cardmember’s. You don’t have to decide which person will ultimately use the miles when you make a purchase. So unlike a consumer card where the miles go into the primary cardmember’s account, these are transferable AAdvantage miles. The Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® also waives American’s small business program’s usual requirements of five active travelers and $5,000 in eligible American Airlines flight spending to access earned miles. That lets you ‘double tip’ with American, earning business program miles and miles from the same travel, and tickets credited to a small business account earn an extra loyalty point per dollar spent too. The AAdvantage Business program awards the company one mile per eligible airfare dollar and registered travelers one additional Loyalty Point per eligible airfare dollar. What You Earn On Purchases The Citi AAdvantage Business Card currently earns: 2 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 2 miles per dollar at gas stations, car rental merchants, telecommunications merchants, and cable and satellite providers. 1 mile per dollar on other purchases. Starting January 24, 2027, the refresh adds 3 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings, plus 2 miles per dollar in one selected category: U.S. shipping providers, office supply stores or U.S. advertising services. The selected business category can be changed quarterly and has no spending cap. Checked Bags, Boarding And The Companion Certificate The primary cardmember and up to four companions on the same reservation receive a first checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries and Group 5 boarding. You don’t have to buy the ticket with this card to receive those benefits. They follow the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage number on the reservation. An employee traveling separately doesn’t get free checked bags or preferred boarding merely from an employee card. After $30,000 in purchases during a cardmembership year and renewal, the primary cardmember can earn a companion certificate for an eligible domestic Main Cabin roundtrip. The companion pays $99 plus taxes and fees. You buy a qualifying Main Cabin ticket, the companion must have eligible fare inventory available, and you book through American Airlines Meeting Services. Travel is generally within the contiguous 48 states, with additional provisions for residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after its anniversary month to receive the certificate. The card also offers 10% savings on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages. What The January 24 Refresh Adds To The Citi AAdvantage Business Card The Citi AAdvantage Business Card annual fee rises by $51, and the biggest latest credit replaces an existing benefit. Up to $100 in inflight credits each calendar year. Eligible food, beverage and paid Wi-Fi purchases replace the current 25% savings on inflight food and beverages and Wi-Fi. This doesn’t cover purchases in Admirals Clubs. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but many readers already have this benefit through another card. 25% off a Melio subscription. This discounts the subscription initiative, not the processing fee charged for paying bills with a credit card. Travel protections. The card adds trip delay, trip cancellation and interruption, lost or damaged luggage, and rental car coverage. Spend $100 on qualifying inflight purchases and the old 25% rebate returned $25. The new credit returns $100, an improvement of $75. After the $51 annual fee increase, you’re $24 ahead on those two changes alone. At $400 in qualifying inflight spending, both versions return $100. Above that, the old uncapped 25% rebate was worth more. I don’t know many people who spent $400 inflight on food and beverages with American Airlines. As I detailed when the changes were declared, business card trip delay coverage is up to $500 per covered trip after an eligible delay exceeding six hours, limited to two claims per account in a 12 month period. It isn’t $500 for each traveler. For trip delay and cancellation or interruption coverage, the full covered trip must be paid with the card or an eligible combination of the card and AAdvantage miles, certificates, vouchers, coupons or discounts. When I’d Put Spending On This Card For $100,000 in purchases outside bonus categories, a 2% cash back card would return $2,000. This card produces 100,000 miles. Put that spending on an eligible employee card and it also produces 100,000 Loyalty Points for each of two people. Whether those miles are worth more or less than $2,000 depends on how you use them. The status credit is what can make this a real winning play and it has more value when two people will use the status. If you’re only interested in redeemable miles, other cards can earn more rewards on ordinary spending, including transferable points. Citi’s Strata Premier nad Strata Elite can earn points faster and transfer to American. The business card makes sense for earning status. The Executive Card Can Make This More Valuable The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] awards 10,000 additional Loyalty Points at each of four thresholds: 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points in a qualification year. You don’t have to earn the qualifying points by spending on the Executive card. Points from business card spending can trigger the bonuses. Suppose the business primary cardmember and one employee each also hold a separate Executive card as a primary cardmember. Then: $105,000 in eligible purchases on that employee’s business card earns each person 105,000 Loyalty Points. Each person’s Executive card adds 20,000 Loyalty Points from the first two thresholds. Each reaches 125,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro and oneworld Emerald. That requires two separate Executive accounts, each with a $695 annual fee, in addition to the business card. I’ve written about doing this with my wife. I already have the business and Executive cards. Giving her an employee card for the business, and having her hold a separate primary Executive card, could help both of us earn oneworld Emerald from the same business spending. For my family, that has a great use. If we’re flying home from Sydney on an eligible oneworld flight, two Emerald members can each bring a guest into the Qantas first class lounge. We’d have access for all four of us even when we’re flying business class.     Sources indicate that when I covered the refresh, American confirmed to me that all Citi AAdvantage Business cardmembers were included after the former Barclays business accounts migrated. This used to be called a targeted promotion because legacy Barclays cardmembers didn’t qualify.

    Here’s what eligible spending on one employee’s card can accomplish in a single status qualification year, assuming neither person earns Loyalty Points elsewhere:.

    American’s qualification year starts March 1 and runs through the end of February. You can combine the card’s Loyalty Points with qualifying activity from other sources.

    Sources indicate that A business owner with several employee cards receives the additional Loyalty Points across their eligible spending. Each employee gets credit for the purchases on their individual card.

    Authorized customers must be employees or contractors of the business, and need to be enrolled in AAdvantage and AAdvantage Business to receive their Loyalty Points. A spouse who works in the business fits this.

    Redeemable miles work differently from status credit. The miles from purchases, including employee purchases, and the initial bonus go into the company’s AAdvantage Business account. The business can then transfer miles to registered travelers’ personal AAdvantage accounts, including the primary cardmember’s. You don’t have to decide which person will ultimately use the miles when you make a purchase. So unlike a consumer card where the miles go into the primary cardmember’s account, these are transferable AAdvantage miles. The Citi® / AAdvantage BusinessTM World Elite Mastercard® also waives American’s small business program’s usual requirements of five active travelers and $5,000 in eligible American Airlines flight spending to access earned miles. That lets you ‘double tip’ with American, earning business program miles and miles from the same travel, and tickets credited to a small business account earn an extra loyalty point per dollar spent too. The AAdvantage Business program awards the company one mile per eligible airfare dollar and registered travelers one additional Loyalty Point per eligible airfare dollar. What You Earn On Purchases The Citi AAdvantage Business Card presently earns: 2 miles per dollar on eligible American Airlines purchases. 2 miles per dollar at gas stations, car rental merchants, telecommunications merchants, and cable and satellite providers. 1 mile per dollar on other purchases. Starting January 24, 2027, the refresh adds 3 miles per dollar on eligible AAdvantage Hotels and AAdvantage Cars bookings, plus 2 miles per dollar in one selected category: U.S. shipping providers, office supply stores or U.S. advertising services. The selected business category can be changed quarterly and has no spending cap. Checked Bags, Boarding And The Companion Certificate The primary cardmember and up to four companions on the same reservation receive a first checked bag free on eligible domestic American Airlines itineraries and Group 5 boarding. You don’t have to buy the ticket with this card to receive those benefits. They follow the primary cardmember’s AAdvantage number on the reservation. An employee traveling separately doesn’t get free checked bags or preferred boarding merely from an employee card. After $30,000 in purchases during a cardmembership year and renewal, the primary cardmember can earn a companion certificate for an eligible domestic Main Cabin roundtrip. The companion pays $99 plus taxes and fees. You buy a qualifying Main Cabin ticket, the companion must have eligible fare inventory available, and you book through American Airlines Meeting Services. Travel is generally within the contiguous 48 states, with additional provisions for residents of Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands. The account must remain open for a full billing cycle after its anniversary month to receive the certificate. The card also offers 10% savings on eligible American Airlines Vacations packages. What The January 24 Refresh Adds To The Citi AAdvantage Business Card The Citi AAdvantage Business Card annual fee rises by $51, and the biggest new credit replaces an existing benefit. Up to $100 in inflight credits each calendar year. Eligible food, beverage and paid Wi-Fi purchases replace the current 25% savings on inflight food and beverages and Wi-Fi. This doesn’t cover purchases in Admirals Clubs. Up to $120 for Global Entry or TSA PreCheck every four years. Useful if you need it, but many readers already have this benefit through another card. 25% off a Melio subscription. This discounts the subscription initiative, not the processing fee charged for paying bills with a credit card. Travel protections. The card adds trip delay, trip cancellation and interruption, lost or damaged luggage, and rental car coverage. Spend $100 on qualifying inflight purchases and the old 25% rebate returned $25. The new credit returns $100, an improvement of $75. After the $51 annual fee increase, you’re $24 ahead on those two changes alone. At $400 in qualifying inflight spending, both versions return $100. Above that, the old uncapped 25% rebate was worth more. I don’t know many people who spent $400 inflight on food and beverages with American Airlines. As I detailed when the changes were announced, business card trip delay coverage is up to $500 per covered trip after an eligible delay exceeding six hours, limited to two claims per account in a 12 month period. It isn’t $500 for each traveler. For trip delay and cancellation or interruption coverage, the full covered trip must be paid with the card or an eligible combination of the card and AAdvantage miles, certificates, vouchers, coupons or discounts. When I’d Put Spending On This Card For $100,000 in purchases outside bonus categories, a 2% cash back card would return $2,000. This card produces 100,000 miles. Put that spending on an eligible employee card and it also produces 100,000 Loyalty Points for each of two people. Whether those miles are worth more or less than $2,000 depends on how you use them. The status credit is what can make this a real winning play and it has more value when two people will use the status. If you’re only interested in redeemable miles, other cards can earn more rewards on ordinary spending, including transferable points. Citi’s Strata Premier nad Strata Elite can earn points faster and transfer to American. The business card makes sense for earning status. The Executive Card Can Make This More Valuable The Citi® / AAdvantage® Executive World Legend Mastercard® [See rates and fees] awards 10,000 additional Loyalty Points at each of four thresholds: 50,000, 90,000, 165,000 and 240,000 Loyalty Points in a qualification year. You don’t have to earn the qualifying points by spending on the Executive card. Points from business card spending can trigger the bonuses. Suppose the business primary cardmember and one employee each also hold a separate Executive card as a primary cardmember. Then: $105,000 in eligible purchases on that employee’s business card earns each person 105,000 Loyalty Points. Each person’s Executive card adds 20,000 Loyalty Points from the first two thresholds. Each reaches 125,000 Loyalty Points, enough for Platinum Pro and oneworld Emerald. That requires two separate Executive accounts, each with a $695 annual fee, in addition to the business card. I’ve written about doing this with my wife. I already have the business and Executive cards. Giving her an employee card for the business, and having her hold a separate primary Executive card, could help both of us earn oneworld Emerald from the same business spending. For my family, that has a great use. If we’re flying home from Sydney on an eligible oneworld flight, two Emerald members can each bring a guest into the Qantas first class lounge. We’d have access for all four of us even when we’re flying business class.     A U.K.-EU Reset Is Bad News for the Special Relationship

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For those of us in Britain who care about democracy, November 20 marked a disturbing political development that Americans should take notice of.
    • According to recent reports, in June 2016, over 17 million Britons voted to leave the European Union and take back control of our lawmaking abilities from Brussels.
    • Joseph Dinnage is senior press officer at the Prosperity Institute.

    For those of us in Britain who care about democracy, November 20 marked a disturbing political development that Americans should take notice of. Prime Minister Andy Burnham traveled to Brussels for the U.K.-EU Summit — a renegotiation of Britain’s trading terms with the EU. Standing alongside the European Union’s chief bureaucrats, Burnham announced a series of deals — concentrating on food standards, youth mobility between Britain and the EU, and carbon and energy trading — that will erect fresh trade barriers between the U.K. and the United States.

    According to recent reports, in June 2016, over 17 million Britons voted to leave the European Union and take back control of our lawmaking abilities from Brussels. The principle of parliamentary sovereignty — the foundation of the British constitution, which holds that Parliament is the supreme lawmaking authority in the land — had been eroded during our membership in the EU as we increasingly outsourced decision-making to unelected foreign bureaucrats. The Brexit vote was a watershed in British politics that allowed us to become the sovereign state we are today.

    Joseph Dinnage is senior press officer at the Prosperity Institute.

    On “A U.K.-EU Reset Is Bad News for the Special Relationship”.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thepointsguy ↗ Open Full Page

    BermudAir adds 18 routes, 10 upcoming cities in massive expansion

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (461 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • BermudAir is making moves to be a major player in the booming market between the U.S.
    • The airline declared a plethora of new routes this past week, marking a major expansion across North American markets, including direct flights to Caribbean destinations.
    • BermudAir will add service from Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY), Nashville International Airport (BNA), Tweed New Haven Airport (HVN) in Connecticut, Burlington International Airport (BTV) in Vermont, Portland International Jetport (PWM) in Maine, San Antonio International Airport (SAT) and Fredericton International Airport (YFC) in New Brunswick, Canada.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    BermudAir is making moves to be a major player in the booming market between the U.S. and the Caribbean.

    The airline declared a plethora of new routes this past week, marking a major expansion across North American markets, including direct flights to Caribbean destinations.

    BermudAir will add service from Louis Armstrong New Orleans International Airport (MSY), Nashville International Airport (BNA), Tweed New Haven Airport (HVN) in Connecticut, Burlington International Airport (BTV) in Vermont, Portland International Jetport (PWM) in Maine, San Antonio International Airport (SAT) and Fredericton International Airport (YFC) in New Brunswick, Canada.

    Industry observers note that those seven join BermudAir's existing North American airports: Newark Liberty International Airport (EWR), Westchester County Airport (HPN) in New York, Boston Logan International Airport (BOS), Baltimore/Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport (BWI), Raleigh-Durham International Airport (RDU), Orlando Sanford International Airport (SFB), St. Pete–Clearwater International Airport (PIE), Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport (FLL), Toronto Pearson International Airport (YYZ), Montréal-Pierre Elliott Trudeau International Airport (YUL) and Halifax Stanfield International Airport (YHZ).

    In a recent development, the airline, meanwhile, is adding to its list of direct and nonstop destinations beyond L.F. Wade International Airport (BDA) in Bermuda, with flights to: Ian Fleming International Airport (OCJ) in Ocho Rios, Jamaica; El Salvador International Airport (SAL) in San Salvador, El Salvador; and Ramón Villeda Morales International Airport (SAP) in San Pedro Sula, Honduras.

    Recent findings suggest that the new airports join BermudAir's roster of previously announced destinations: Clayton J. Lloyd International Airport (AXA) in Anguilla; Philip S.W. Goldson International Airport (BZE) in Belize; Owen Roberts International Airport (GCM) in Grand Cayman; La Aurora International Airport (GUA) in Guatemala; and Providenciales International Airport (PLS) in Turks and Caicos. The airline also offers flights to and from its Bermuda hub.

    Recent findings suggest that "2027 represents an exciting newly introduced chapter for BermudAir," Adam Scott, BermudAir's founder and CEO, noted in a statement. "We're bringing our distinctive brand of premium leisure travel to more cities and opening up more opportunities for travelers to experience Bermuda, the Caribbean and Central America.".

    While it is typically difficult for an airline to fly between two countries that are not the airline's home nation, BermudAir notes that it plans to operate the routes as fifth freedom flights originating in Bermuda, Turks and Caicos, Grand Cayman or Anguilla — all British Overseas Territories, which appears to satisfy regulatory statutes.

    BermudAir launched in 2023 as a boutique carrier that planned to run flights between Bermuda and North America using small and efficient Embraer jets. It launched its first flights between North America and other destinations as part of its winter 2026-27 schedule.

    The airline's expansion has been rapid, and if successful, the new routes would make BermudAir a regional force in the Caribbean leisure market.

    #169841. Hyatt Regency LAX Caps Stays At 21 Days—The Legal Risk That Makes Hotels Turn Away Paying Guests

    📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5323 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Viewfromthewing ↗ Open Full Page

    Hyatt Regency LAX Caps Stays At 21 Days—The Legal Risk That Makes Hotels Turn Away Paying Guests

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5323 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hyatt Regency LAX won’t let you stay more than 21 consecutive days.
    • They seem to be worried about a guest becoming a tenant under the law.
    • The hotel does not accept reservations that result in a guest staying more than 21 consecutive days, whether through one reservation or multiple back-to-back reservations.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hyatt Regency LAX won’t let you stay more than 21 consecutive days. Booking separate reservations won’t get around it. The hotel even counts back-to-back stays. They seem to be worried about a guest becoming a tenant under the law. A customer who wants to keep paying can become someone the hotel needs to turn away. The published policy claims: The hotel does not accept reservations that result in a guest staying more than 21 consecutive days, whether through one reservation or multiple back-to-back reservations. Meanwhile, its frequently asked questions advertises “Extended Stay Regency Suites” and tells guests to contact the property about extended stays or special arrangements. Apparently there’s extended, and then there’s too extended. Why A Hotel Might Want You Gone Before A Month I’d put 90% odds at avoiding residential tenancy exposure being the main explanation for this policy. Once someone qualifies as a tenant, ending their stay can require notices and a court eviction instead of ordinary hotel checkout procedures. Depending on the jurisdiction and property, rent regulation and restrictions on the grounds for eviction can enter the picture, too. The hotel may have to spend money establishing that an exception applies before it can get its room back. In the city of Los Angeles, the rent stabilization ordinance brings hotel accommodations occupied as someone’s primary residence for more than 30 days into its definition of a rental unit. Building age and other exemptions matter, too, though. California also has a separate exclusion for qualifying hotels that retain access and control and offer a specified set of services, including housekeeping, mail and room services. The relevant Los Angeles threshold is 30 days. A 21 day limit looks like a conservative buffer, leaving room to deal with a delayed departure before getting close to it. Although a hotel might want to preserve rooms for shorter, more profitable bookings, or limit payment risk. Other Hotels Have Limits, Including Right Next To California In Vegas Hyatt Regency LAX isn’t alone. Here are published limits at some other properties: Hotel Published Stay Limit Hyatt Regency Valencia 28 days Hyatt Regency Westlake 28 days Best Western Los Angeles Worldport, Wilmington 28 days The LINE Los Angeles 29 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 Wynn Las Vegas / Encore Terms state a 14 day maximum for all reservations Oasis at Gold Spike, Las Vegas 14 consecutive nights The LINE Austin 29 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 The LINE Washington, D.C. 28 days, contact the hotel for stays over 21 The legal differences at play: Nevada has a 30 day trigger. Its residential landlord-tenant statute excludes hotel or motel occupancy of less than 30 consecutive days, unless the occupant clearly reveals an intent to remain for a longer continuous period. Texas looks at the relationship between property and guest. As Texas Legal Aid explains, length of stay, payment arrangements, contract terms, housekeeping and control of the room all help distinguish a guest from a tenant. The state’s 30 day hotel tax exemption also applies. Florida gives the written agreement more weight. Its current definition treats hotel and motel occupancy as transient unless a written rental or lease agreement expressly says the unit is the guest’s sole residence. Transient hotel occupancy is excluded from the residential tenancy chapter. New York has more than one route to protection. State law includes a nontransient hotel resident in possession for at least 30 consecutive days within its tenant definition for eviction proceedings. But in a New York City hotel covered by rent stabilization, a guest can acquire permanent tenant status much sooner simply by requesting a qualifying lease. Sometimes A Stay Limit Doesn’t Solve The Problem A hotel can’t necessarily make tenancy law disappear by putting a checkout date in its terms. California prohibits a residential hotel from requiring an occupant to move, or check out and re-register, before 30 days when a purpose is keeping them legally transient. That rule applies to residential hotels, not automatically to every hotel. Los Angeles also counts forced room changes and checkouts intended to avoid its rent-stabilization rules. New York City’s rules for covered hotels go further. An occupant who’s never had a lease can request one at any point during occupancy. The request makes them a permanent tenant, and the owner must provide a lease of at least six months within 15 days. The rules also prohibit refusing to continue a tenancy solely to prevent permanent-tenant status. In that setting, a claim can arise after the first night. I understand preventing an apartment landlord from evading the law by calling the building a hotel. But making it difficult for an actual hotel and a willing customer to agree on a temporary stay has costs, too. Someone working on a project, waiting for a home repair, or staying near a hospital may want six weeks of housekeeping and a front desk. They don’t necessarily want an apartment lease. If accommodating that person creates a costly risk of being unable to recover the room, the hotel has an incentive to refuse the booking. The New Yorker Guest Tried To Take The Whole Building The Wyndham New Yorker case I’ve covered took these risks to their absurd extreme. Mickey Barreto booked one night in 2018 for $149 plus tax, requested a lease, and wouldn’t leave. After the hotel removed him, he went to housing court and obtained an order restoring possession of his room. And the hotel subsequently lost a contested eviction case and its appeal. To establish the exemption it claimed from rent stabilization, the property needed to prove that the room rented for more than $350 a month or $88 a week on May 31, 1968. In 2020, an appellate court upheld the eviction case’s dismissal because the hotel hadn’t supplied sufficient evidence. A 1966 hotel directory and a 1969 accountant’s report didn’t establish the necessary room rate on the statutory date. Imagine trying to get your hotel room back in 2020 and losing because you can’t adequately document what it cost in 1968. While the room dispute was going on, Barreto treated his possession order as a basis to claim the entire building. His theory was that the property hadn’t been subdivided, so rights to his room somehow gave him the hotel. He filed documents purporting to transfer ownership to himself and his nonprofit, Mickey Barreto Missions. According to Manhattan prosecutors, he demanded rent from a tenant, demanded control of the hotel’s bank accounts, told the real owner to leave, and approached Wyndham about transferring the franchise. He even went to its lenders to try to borrow against the property. The city recorded fraudulent documents. The courts protected possession of a room. A 2019 judgment declared the deed void and confirmed the real owner’s title. He nevertheless made further false filings in 2023. Tenancy law didn’t authorize stealing a skyscraper. But the hotel was already fighting over a one night guest’s right to remain when it had to start defending its title, its accounts and its dealings with tenants and lenders, too. Barreto was finally evicted in 2024. In February 2026, nearly eight years after checking in, he pleaded guilty to fraud. His sentence was six months already served and five years of probation. In 2020, an appellate court upheld the eviction case’s dismissal because the hotel hadn’t supplied sufficient evidence. A 1966 hotel directory and a 1969 accountant’s report didn’t establish the necessary room rate on the statutory date. Imagine trying to get your hotel room back in 2020 and losing because you can’t adequately document what it cost in 1968. While the room dispute was going on, Barreto treated his possession order as a basis to claim the entire building. His theory was that the property hadn’t been subdivided, so rights to his room somehow gave him the hotel. He filed documents purporting to transfer ownership to himself and his nonprofit, Mickey Barreto Missions. According to Manhattan prosecutors, he demanded rent from a tenant, demanded control of the hotel’s bank accounts, told the real owner to leave, and approached Wyndham about transferring the franchise. He even went to its lenders to try to borrow against the property. The city recorded fraudulent documents. The courts protected possession of a room. A 2019 judgment declared the deed void and confirmed the real owner’s title. He nevertheless made further false filings in 2023. Tenancy law didn’t authorize stealing a skyscraper.     Fake Amex Black Cards For $1,000—People Are Buying Status, But They May Be Committing A Crime

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1893 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, A man apparently made a fortune selling fake American Express Black Cards for about $1,000 apiece.
    • Recent findings suggest that that’s the story told in this viral clip from Inside True Crime.
    • A post shared by Matthew Cox | Inside True Crime (@insidetruecrime).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, A man apparently made a fortune selling fake American Express Black Cards for about $1,000 apiece. The cards used buyers’ real account numbers, so when they paid for items the charges went onto their own bills. They were buying the appearance of being a Centurion cardmember. That’s the story told in this viral clip from Inside True Crime. His claim that customers could simply flash the cards to get into airport lounges is a lot harder to square with reality. View this post on Instagram.

    Recent findings suggest that that’s the story told in this viral clip from Inside True Crime. His claim that customers could simply flash the cards to get into airport lounges is a lot harder to square with reality.

    A post shared by Matthew Cox | Inside True Crime (@insidetruecrime).

    Cox claims the man put customers’ existing American Express numbers onto cards that looked like Centurion cards. They could pay for things, impress a date, and supposedly get waved into exclusive spaces. He says the business went on for years.

    The comments split between people asking what the crime was, people asking where to order one, and frequent travelers pointing out that lounge access isn’t granted based on the look of the card – they run it through their system.

    It has been revealed that I’ve covered this sort of thing for years. Back in 2015, I wrote about a company that would turn an existing credit card into a custom metal card. Prices started at $99, with custom designs at $149 and gold plating at $249. That service couldn’t handle payment chips at the time. The payment system charges the account identified by the card’s credentials. Changing the material or artwork doesn’t change the rewards, spending power, or benefits attached to that account. And American Express itself has experimented with the physical form. In 2021, I covered artist-designed Centurion cards and a Prada wearable. Those were options Amex provided to real Centurion members. The Airport Lounge Claim Isn’t Plausible The reel makes a weird claim. It notes the black card “doesn’t work,” then says it can pay for things. In the longer discussion, he means it doesn’t acquire the spending power he associates with a real Black Card. More importantly, Centurion Lounge access belongs to eligible cardmembers. A Gold account dressed up as Centurion is still a Gold account when its eligibility is checked. It hasn’t acquired lounge access, Centurion access priority, or any other benefit. Paying Your Own Bill Doesn’t Make It Legal The comments ask “what’s the crime?” Using someone else’s account to steal money is different from paying your own restaurant bill with a customized card. But there are several separate issues here. The maker copying Amex branding. Selling a replica with American Express branding raises trademark infringement issues. The concern is whether it falsely appears to be an Amex-issued or approved product. Depending on the marks and conduct, criminal trademark counterfeiting can also apply. The customer paying normally. An altered card isn’t automatically federal credit card fraud. The federal access-device statute includes altered and counterfeit cards, but requires intent to defraud. Merely wanting a date to think you’re rich isn’t enough. The customer claiming benefits they haven’t earned. Passing off the card as proof of Centurion membership to obtain restricted lounge services, a waived fee, or another benefit creates a different problem. It’s not obvious this would even work. And paying the bar tab doesn’t pay for the separate service obtained through deception. Using the fake credential to support false claims in a credit transaction would be a separate problem. Several state laws could be implicated. Texas has separate credit card, forgery, and counterfeit card rules. And Amex’s October 2023 U.S. merchant regulations instructed merchants not to accept a card that appeared physically altered. Getting a transaction approved doesn’t prove the replacement card was authorized, even if the merchant doesn’t know. Banks spend money on cards that look and feel good. Paying $1,000 to pretend you have a different one is an expensive way to impress someone who’s watching you pay. That’s more than the $895 first year’s annual fee on an actual Platinum Card, which comes with actual Centurion Lounge access. The card just wouldn’t be black.     #169839. Sweeping permitting overhaul passes Senate, on to House

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1482 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Sweeping permitting overhaul passes Senate, on to House

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1482 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, from left, Sens.
    • The Senate passed a bill Thursday evening that would overhaul the federal permitting system for electric power lines, power lines wind and solar farms, hard rock mining and oil drilling projects and more.
    • According to recent reports, it's the culmination of a yearslong effort intended to address industry concerns that it is too difficult to build any major infrastructure project in the United States.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, from left, Sens. Mike Lee, R-Utah., Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., and Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., hold a news conference on the measure in the Capitol on Sept. 30. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    The Senate passed a bill Thursday evening that would overhaul the federal permitting system for electric power lines, power lines wind and solar farms, hard rock mining and oil drilling projects and more.

    According to recent reports, it's the culmination of a yearslong effort intended to address industry concerns that it is too difficult to build any major infrastructure project in the United States. Supporters overcame opposition from more than half the Democratic Caucus, which will be a factor when the bill moves to the House after the Thanksgiving recess.

    The bill passed on a 62-33 vote, with 31 Democrats joining two Republicans, Josh Hawley of Missouri and Mike Rounds of South Dakota, in opposition.

    Shortly after the post-cloture time expired late Thursday, the Senate voted on passage of the legislation, including a substitute amendment consisting of revised text of the original permitting bill that the bipartisan authors unveiled before the midterm elections.

    However, the chamber did not consider any additional amendments to the bill, as initially planned by the sponsors, including Environment and Public Works Chairman Shelley Moore Capito, R-W.Va., panel ranking member Sheldon Whitehouse, D-R.I., Energy and Natural Resources Chairman Mike Lee, R-Utah, and panel ranking member Martin Heinrich, D-N.M.

    The bill includes changes to how reviews are conducted and permits are issued under the National Environmental Policy Act, National Historic Preservation Act, Endangered Species Act, Federal Power Act and Clean Water Act.

    It includes provisions intended to ensure electricity ratepayers are not saddled with the costs of bringing power to data centers, and would give the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission fresh authority over interstate transmission lines.

    Sources indicate that it also would provide legal recourse when administrations discriminate against certain forms of energy or seek to revisit permits on ideological grounds. That's intended in part to address the Trump administration’s actions to delay or block solar and wind energy projects.

    It has been revealed that democrats walked away from negotiations last year due to Trump administration actions to block offshore wind construction. However they ultimately said they received sufficient assurances that the administration would let stalled wind and solar projects move forward.

    The "big four" senators on the permitting bill solicited feedback and changes sought by various lawmakers on both sides of the aisle, and were open to votes on additional amendments — so long as they didn't undo the measure's core tenets.

    "This bill has threaded a needle the likes of which this chamber has not seen in a while, and we’ve got to take advantage of this opportunity," Capito mentioned before passage.

    Industry observers note that ultimately, Oregon Democratic Sens. Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden would not consent to a time agreement allowing consideration of a finite number of amendments because Republicans wouldn't allow up-or-down votes at a simple-majority threshold on some of theirs. Merkley then objected to a unanimous consent request to consider amendments on the floor.

    Wyden was pushing for a vote on an amendment that would prohibit construction of data centers on federal public lands. Merkley was pushing for amendments that included barring data centers from benefiting from “project certainty” protections against future presidents revoking their permits, and limiting presidential power to impose tariffs on clean energy project components, like wind turbines.

    The Senate had already adopted the substitute amendment introduced by the bill’s sponsors during a procedural vote on Wednesday. But the lack of a unanimous consent agreement to take up more amendments meant that an additional manager's package of changes to the substitute fell by the wayside.

    That amendment would have narrowed the instances where exemptions from National Historic Preservation Act reviews would be allowed, increased the annual authorization for the Historic Preservation Fund by 50 percent, and addressed concerns about the use of eminent domain when permitting transmission projects raised by Hawley and Rounds.

    The sponsors introduced an updated version of their manager’s amendment Thursday afternoon that would refine exemptions from the ratepayer projection provisions so that artificial intelligence "hyperscalers" can't escape through a loophole.

    The original manager's amendment sought to exempt internet and telecommunications providers' facilities, but the language was broad enough that cloud storage and other "information services" exclusions could potentially benefit data centers.

    None of those changes made it into the bill as a result of the stalemate over amendments, and Merkley objected on the floor to incorporating just the manager's package.

    It has been revealed that the bill has been endorsed by a wide range of industry groups, who argue that the current federal permitting regime makes it too difficult to finance, proposal and construct projects domestically. This includes the American Petroleum Institute, the American Clean Power Association, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and the National Association of Manufacturers.

    The White House expressed its support for the bill in a statement of administration policy this month.

    The bill now moves on to the House, where it seemingly has the votes to pass.

    Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., said last week that the bill can pass in that chamber, while a number of Democrats including the centrist Blue Dog Coalition and Reps. Scott Peters, D-Calif., co-chair of the bipartisan Climate Solutions Caucus, and Nikki Budzinski, D-Ill., have expressed support.

    Budzinski was elected chair of the 112-member New Democrat Coalition last week for the next Congress, and that group issued a statement speaking favorably of permitting while stopping short of endorsing the bill as presently drafted.

    However, attendance on the House GOP side after Thanksgiving could be an matter: more than 30 lawmakers regularly skipped votes this week, the majority of them Republicans.

    And many Democrats have called on Heinrich and Whitehouse to punt consideration of the bill to the new Congress, when their party will have large majorities in both chambers.

    Merkley, who is in line to chair the Environment and Public Works Committee, and House Natural Resources ranking member Jared Huffman, D-Calif. — the expected chairman of that panel — both said the bill included too many provisions Democrats opposed in order to garner Republican support.

    Industry observers note that some of the nation’s largest environmental groups including the Sierra Club and Natural Resources Defense Council oppose the bill. A coalition of 17 Democratic states also expressed their opposition. And some Native American tribes and organizations, including the National Congress of American Indians, also expressed their opposition.

    "I’m hoping to have a full opportunity to address the many legitimate concerns that stakeholders have raised with this bill," Merkley said before the vote Thursday night.

    But Heinrich and Whitehouse resisted calls to delay the bill, arguing that President Donald Trump is in office for two more years and that any bill needs his support to be signed into law. They added that they will be able to address environmental complications under their majority, and that this bill would represent the “floor” of their ambitions.

    While Republicans have called for changes to the federal permitting system for decades, the effort gained steam with Democrats after the passage of their 2022 reconciliation law, which they dubbed the Inflation Reduction Act, or IRA.

    As part of the deal to get then-Senate Energy and Natural Resources Chairman Joe Manchin III, D-W.Va., on board with the IRA, the Biden administration agreed to support a bill overhauling the federal permitting system. Manchin introduced a bill that included changes to NEPA and transmission permitting, and would approve all remaining permits needed for the Mountain Valley Pipeline in his home state.

    However, his effort ultimately fell short on a 47-47 procedural vote to attach the bill to that year’s defense authorization measure.

    In the 118th Congress Manchin tried again, and in 2024 he and then-Energy and Natural Resources ranking member John Barrasso, R-Wyo., introduced what Manchin called a “perfectly crafted balance.” The committee approved that bill in July 2024, but it was never voted on by the full Senate.

    Capito, Whitehouse, Lee and Heinrich made a collective commitment to address permitting overhaul when they stepped into their current roles in January 2025, and spent nearly 21 months working on the legislation.

    Since Manchin’s first bill, the political calculus changed.

    Recent findings suggest that after decades of stagnant energy demand, electricity prices began rising in part due to the expansion of data centers. Consumers also became increasingly frustrated with their local utilities over affordability concerns, which in turn spurred more lawmakers across the country, including on Capitol Hill, to critically examine their practices.

    Lee also pushed for language streamlining NHPA reviews, which had not been a focus of earlier permitting discussion. He's argued that the law has expanded beyond its originally intended scope and become a major barrier to infrastructure projects in Western states like Utah.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    With new high-efficiency residential and commercial modules and an integrated supply chain spanning polysilicon to power conversion, Mission Solar Energy is making a case for U.S. manufacturing, domestic content and FEOC-compliant sourcing.

    Sources indicate that as the solar industry continues to navigate shifting trade policies, domestic content incentives, and supply chain scrutiny, Mission Solar Energy is bringing a message of manufacturing strength and transparency to RE+ 2026. The San Antonio-based manufacturer showcased its latest commercial and residential modules while highlighting the advantages of its relationship with fellow OCI Holdings subsidiaries OCI TerraSus and OCI Power.

    The announcement puts the spotlight on a growing priority for solar developers, installers and distributors: knowing exactly where components originate and having the documentation to prove it.

    In a recent development, the three companies collectively cover significant portions of the solar value chain. OCI TerraSus produces high-purity, solar-grade polysilicon in Sarawak, Malaysia; Mission Solar designs, engineers, and assembles modules in San Antonio, Texas; and OCI Power manufactures inverters and power conversion systems in South Korea.

    According to Mission Solar, all three companies are compliant with Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) requirements and are not classified as prohibited foreign entities. The integrated structure offers customers access to a traceable supply chain backed by OCI Holdings, a global clean energy group headquartered in Seoul.

    For an industry that’s becoming more and more focused on sourcing eligibility and domestic manufacturing credentials, that positioning could prove commercially key.

    On the product front, Mission Solar is highlighting two modules aimed at different market segments.

    Recent findings suggest that for commercial and industrial (C&I) applications, the company is featuring its 595W N-Type Bifacial 144HC module. The dual-glass design captures sunlight from both sides, potentially increasing energy production without requiring additional project footprint. Designed and assembled in the United States, the module carries 11.5% domestic content, meets FEOC requirements and supports front-side loads of up to 5,400 Pa.

    Residential installers will get a look at the 440W N-Type 108HC rooftop module, which Mission Solar says will be the first of its kind on the market with 12% domestic content. Building on an existing 6% domestic-content version, the module combines N-type cell technology and a multi-busbar design to deliver efficiency of up to 23%. It is also approved on residential financing platforms including LightReach and GoodLeap.

    Looking further ahead, Mission Solar aims to preview two next-generation G12R modules, with commercial launches anticipated in late 2027. The organization will also display a lower-domestic-content U.S.-produced C&I module option expected in 2027.

    Although module performance is still critical to the industry, supply chain credibility is increasingly part of the overall purchasing decision.

    As developers evaluate project economics, tax credit eligibility and sourcing risk, manufacturers that can offer transparent documentation alongside competitive technology may have an advantage.

    In a recent development, to relieve stress nowadays, modern high school students may fire up a game of Grand Theft Auto VI or bring a puppy dog to class. But in the recent past, American high schools would set aside a patch of blacktop where tense teenagers could fire up a couple of heaters between classes, presumably so nobody would show up to fourth-period algebra in nicotine withdrawal. Understanding that there was nothing they could do to prevent kids from lighting up, schools in the 1970s and 1980s frequently had smoking courts. The calculation was that they might as well keep the students in their line of sight.

    In those days, airplane passengers could light up while in flight, swathing 150 strangers inside a metal tube at 30,000 feet in Pall Mall smoke from Milwaukee to Phoenix.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, sens. Susan Collins, R-Maine, left, and Mitch McConnell , R-Ky., won't be smiling as much if Democrats force a punt on spending bills to next year. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

    Recent findings suggest that newly released Senate appropriations bills would distribute $8.7 billion in "congressionally directed spending" secured by 78 senators for their home states — earmarked dollars that could disappear if Congress resorts to a stopgap funding measure to avert a partial government shutdown after Dec. 11.

    Nearly 4,000 individual earmarks are contained in nine of the 12 draft fiscal 2027 spending bills, a CQ Roll Call tally found; the remaining three bills — Defense, State-Foreign Operations and Legislative Branch — don't have any.

    There's typically some overlap between House and Senate projects that would get weeded out in final negotiations to avoid duplication. But for comparison's sake, House Republicans included nearly 6,700 line items worth $8.2 billion in their earmarked spending bills.

    Democrats have signaled they'll push for a continuing resolution into the first quarter of next year enabling them to rewrite the full-year fiscal 2027 bills when they take the gavels in January, possibly upping the overall pot of earmarked funds — or at least divvying up the pie more favorably to blue states and districts.

    But that would mean the final attempt by departing lawmakers like Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, and longtime Senate GOP leader and senior appropriator Mitch McConnell of Kentucky, to deliver for their states might be all for naught.

    And top Democrats with substantial earmarking success under GOP governance, such as Appropriations ranking member Patty Murray, D-Wash., will have to start from scratch.

    Here are some key stats on senators' earmarks in the latest batch of spending bills Collins is trying to get across the finish line.

    It has been revealed that naturally, much of the spoils go to Senate Appropriations Committee members, and that's no different this year. But with so many more Democrats requesting projects — often jointly with their fellow delegation member — individual contributions may appear diluted given they have to share the credit.

    That dilution shows up in the rankings when allocating credit in a way that avoids double-counting — everyone gets an equal share of his or her joint projects, so $20 million sponsored jointly by two senators will appear as $10 million for each. Solo earmarkers in this scenario face no such dilution.

    Using the even-split methodology, the top 10 — all senior appropriators — look like this:.

    Another way to look at it is by simply adding up every instance of a senator affixing his or her name to a project, which leads to double-counting but gives them full credit for every earmark secured, even with jointly requested projects.

    Here's the top 10 in that scenario:.

    Finally, there's the solo earmarker leaderboard, only counting dollars secured without any co-sponsors:.

    McConnell and Collins hit the trifecta, ending up among the top three in all three scenarios.

    Related: Maine senators at odds over credit for earmarks.

    Unlike the House, where states with the largest populations receive the most funding by virtue of having more representatives securing earmarks, smaller states punch above their weight in the Senate — particularly when their delegations achieve exalted positions of seniority.

    Hence Washington state — with Murray and Cantwell, the Commerce Committee ranking member, representing it — is way out in front.

    According to recent reports, by contrast, the second- and third-most populous states — Texas and Florida — received a grand total of zero earmarked funds, because their GOP senators didn't request any. California, with the largest population, is No. 16 in the ranks; Latest York is 12th.

    Here are the top 10 states by earmarked funds procured in the Senate bills, clearly skewing toward smaller, typically reddish states:.

    Sources indicate that the Transportation-HUD spending bill continues to be the go-to place for earmarks, accounting for 27 percent of all individual projects in the Senate bills and about one-third of all the earmarked dollars. The next-closest bill, Labor-HHS-Education, has half the earmarked amount that the "T-HUD" bill does.

    Top agencies and programs with earmarked funds are housed within, that's right, the departments of Transportation and Housing and Urban Development, with HUD leading the pack thanks to its ever-popular Community Development Fund accounting for all of that department's earmarks.

    Transportation isn't far behind, thanks largely to highway projects, followed by Health and Human Services and its Health Resources and Services Administration account, which funds community health centers. Defense Department military construction projects and the Army Corps of Engineers round out the group of $1 billion-plus agencies.

    Here are the top accounts for earmarked funds in this year's crop of bills:.

    The biggest individual earmarks are largely within Army Corps accounts funded in the draft Energy-Water bill, with some military construction and transportation projects and two mega NIST-based university construction earmarks thrown in on behalf of Collins and McConnell.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On the last day before the 2026 midterm elections, President Donald Trump gave a speech before the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a site of considerable scandal in his second term. He joked it should be renamed after him and spent considerable time discussing Washington, D.C. construction projects and resurrecting conspiracy theories about monument vandals. When the president did turn to the elections, more than 23 minutes into an hour-long speech, he seemed to foreshadow major Republican losses in the House and Senate, describing it as “The most important midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.”.

    “When you vote, remember a party that hates America cannot be allowed to rule over the people who built our country,” Trump noted, referring to Democrats, whom he said want to “blow all of this up by electing communist jihadists.”.

    Sources indicate that “If the people that voted for me and voted in the last election where we had such a great victory, if they go out and vote, just a good portion of them, we will win in a landslide,” Trump said midway in his speech. “Now that doesn’t happen because usually whoever the sitting president is, Republican or Democrat, uh, good or bad, good president, great president, bad, for some reason the sitting president doesn’t win the midterms, but we gave this a very strong shot.”.

    Industry observers note that the last day of polling indicates that Democrats have odds that are better than good to flip control of the House and Senate. The final results from the New York Times/Siena University polls report “The party is ahead in all seven states likeliest to decide control of the Senate: Michigan, Kansas, Texas, Maine, Ohio and, more narrowly, Alaska and Iowa.” The final predictions in the Cook Political Report included five additional shifts for Democrats in North Carolina, Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, projecting “that Democrats will win 15 to 25 seats, putting them at a 230- to 240-seat majority.” If a sweep happens in the toss up races, it’ll give Democrats their strongest majority since 2009.

    Meanwhile, early voting records have been smashed around the country, in places like South Carolina and Ohio. In Texas, more than 7.7 million voters did so early, surpassing the record turnout for a midterm election set in 2018. Across the nation, about 50 million ballots have already been cast so far, with the share of registered Democrats notably increased in several key state races. But according to the New York Times, around half the expected votes will come on Election Day itself, making it difficult at this point to determine how substantial a role early votes will play in the outcome.

    #169830. Sacha Baron Cohen reveals “Who Is America?” and the answer is terrifying

    📅 16 Jul 2018 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1875 w)
